segments.text: Morning. Standup. Same shape as always: what you did, what's next, blockers. Then decisions since last time, then stale commitments. Priya, go.
Okay. Done: the payments service API spec went out Thursday the 10th, Rahul has it.
Got it, already stubbed.
In progress: the UPI flow. And... this is where I have bad news. It's going to slip.
How much?
The Razorpay sandbox doesn't fire the UPI collect callbacks reliably. I lost Thursday and Friday on webhook signature verification before I realised it was their side, not mine.
So I need to move it to Friday. Friday the 25th, instead of the 24th.
One day. Okay. Is the 25th real, or is that hopeful?
It's real. I have a workaround, I poll their status API instead of waiting for the callback. It's ugly but it works.
Fine. UPI flow moves to the 25th. Noted. Blockers?
No. The sandbox keys came on time, thanks.
Rahul.
Done: the offline mode spike. Finished it Friday, so ahead of the 18th.
Nice. Verdict?
SQLite plus a sync queue works, like I hoped. Writes queue locally, replay on reconnect, a hundred records in under a second.
The hard part is conflicts. When two agents edit the same inspection while offline.
Is that actually likely? Two people on the same record?
Meridian says agents share territories, so yeah, sometimes.
So, new commitment from me: I'll bring a sync conflict resolution proposal to the design review on Wednesday the 16th.
Good. Shell?
Shell's on track for tomorrow. Tab bar is in, four tabs, it's ugly but it navigates.
Blockers?
One question, not a blocker. Does offline mode need to cover payments too, or just the forms and inspections? It changes the queue design a lot.
From my side I'd really rather it didn't. Offline payments is a nightmare.
I don't know yet. I asked Meridian on Friday and they didn't have an answer. Park it, I'll chase them. It stays open.
Okay. I'll design the queue so it can go either way.
Sana.
Onboarding screens. Three of five done, on track for the 19th.
I'm changing the tour to three cards instead of five, like Aditya asked on the thread. The agents won't read five.
Good. Blockers?
Not a blocker, but Meridian sent over an accessibility checklist after your call. It's stricter than I expected. Minimum touch targets, screen reader order, that kind of thing.
Yeah, that's from their compliance people. Does it affect us?
Maybe. I want to check the tab bar against it on their five inch devices. I'll have the navigation accessibility review done for Wednesday's design review.
Wait, is the tab bar at risk? I just built it.
I don't know yet. Let me check before I say anything.
Fair. Wednesday, then. Okay, me. The Meridian requirements call happened on Friday the 11th.
Three things came out of it. One, the pilot starts October 20th, three hundred agents. So the 16th really is the date.
Two, decision: the pilot is Android only. iOS moves to November. Their devices are all Android, so there's no point.
Good, one less thing.
Three, receipts. An in-app receipt is fine, no printing. Priya, that was your question.
Perfect. That saves me a week.
Decisions since kickoff: the Android-only one, nothing else. Stale commitments: everything from kickoff is either done or has a date. The UPI flow is the only one that moved.
And the offline payments question stays open. That's on me.
Anything else? No? Okay. Design review Wednesday at ten. Bring the accessibility thing, Sana.
Will do.
Bye.
